title: 亚马逊 CEO 如何谈 AI 对工作和岗位的影响（2025）
topic: 准确转述 AI 对岗位的预期、影响的不确定性和员工行动建议

source.title: Update from Amazon CEO Andy Jassy on Generative AI
source.license: 原文按项目方确认的授权收录
source.context: 原文出自 Amazon 亚马逊 公开资料。
paragraphs: We will need fewer people doing some of the jobs that are being done today, and more people doing other types of jobs. It’s hard to know exactly where this nets out over time, but in the next few years, we expect that this will reduce our total corporate workforce as we get efficiency gains from using AI extensively across the company.

As we go through this transformation together, be curious about AI, educate yourself, attend workshops and take trainings, use and experiment with AI whenever you can, participate in your team’s brainstorms to figure out how to invent for our customers more quickly and expansively, and how to get more done with scrappier teams.

Those who embrace this change, become conversant in AI, help us build and improve our AI capabilities internally and deliver for customers, will be well-positioned to have high impact and help us reinvent the company.
translations: 我们将需要更少的人从事目前的一些工作，也会需要更多的人从事其他类型的工作。很难确切判断长期下来最终会是什么结果；但我们预计，未来几年，随着全公司广泛使用 AI 获得效率提升，企业员工总数会减少。
在共同经历这场转型时，请对 AI 保持好奇，主动学习，参加研讨会和培训，尽可能使用并尝试 AI，参加团队讨论，思考如何更快、更广泛地为客户创造新体验，以及如何用更精干的团队完成更多工作。
拥抱这一变化、熟悉 AI、帮助公司在内部建设和改进 AI 能力并为客户交付价值的人，将更有机会产生重要影响，并帮助公司重塑自身。
fullTextParagraphs: The message below was shared with Amazon employees earlier today.

Today, in virtually every corner of the company, we’re using Generative AI to make customers' lives better and easier. What started as deep conviction that every customer experience would be reinvented using AI, and that altogether new experiences we’ve only dreamed of would become possible, is rapidly becoming reality. Technologies like Generative AI are rare; they come about once-in-a-lifetime, and completely change what’s possible for customers and businesses. So, we are investing quite expansively, and, the progress we are making is evident.

You can see it in what we're rolling out in Alexa+, our next generation Alexa personal assistant that's meaningfully smarter, more capable, and is the first personal assistant that can take significant actions for customers on top of providing intelligent answers to virtually any question.
You can see it with our AI shopping assistant that’s being used by tens of millions of customers around the world to discover new products and make more informed purchase decisions.

You can see it in an increasing array of shopping features like “Lens” (very cool to be able to take a picture of an item and have it pull up the shopping result), “Buy for Me” (where I can ask our shopping agent to buy an item on another merchant’s website for me), or Recommended Size (where we can predict the right size for you based on prior purchases and how different apparel brands run fit-wise relative to each other).

You can see it in how we're helping our independent sellers more easily create new product detail pages or get advice on how to be even more effective as a seller in our marketplace. Nearly half a million selling partners are using these services, and the listings they’re creating are measurably better.

You can see it in Advertising where we’ve built a suite of AI tools that make it easier for brands to plan, onboard, create and optimize campaigns. In Q1 alone, over 50K advertisers used these capabilities.

And, you can see it in what we’re delivering in AWS for builders, whether it’s custom silicon (Trainium2) to provide better price-performance on model-training and inference, services that make it much easier to build Foundation Models (SageMaker), or leverage leading frontier models and do GenAI inference at scale (Bedrock), our own frontier model (Nova) to give customers leading intelligence at lower latency and cost, or services to make it much easier for developers to write code (Q and QCLI).

We’re also using Generative AI broadly across our internal operations. In our fulfillment network, we’re using AI to improve inventory placement, demand forecasting, and the efficiency of our robots—all of which have improved cost to serve and delivery speed. We’ve rebuilt our Customer Service Chatbot with GenAI, providing an even better experience than we’d had before. And, we’re assembling more intelligent and compelling product detail pages from leveraging GenAI.
I could go on, but you get the idea.
While we’ve made a lot of progress, we’re still at the relative beginning. There are a few reasons we believe this and want to go even faster.

First, we have strong conviction that AI agents will change how we all work and live. Think of agents as software systems that use AI to perform tasks on behalf of users or other systems. Agents let you tell them what you want (often in natural language), and do things like scour the web (and various data sources) and summarize results, engage in deep research, write code, find anomalies, highlight interesting insights, translate language and code into other variants, and automate a lot of tasks that consume our time. There will be billions of these agents, across every company and in every imaginable field. There will also be agents that routinely do things for you outside of work, from shopping to travel to daily chores and tasks. Many of these agents have yet to be built, but make no mistake, they’re coming, and coming fast.

Second, and what makes this agentic future so compelling for Amazon, is that these agents are going to change the scope and speed at which we can innovate for customers. Agents will allow us to start almost everything from a more advanced starting point. We’ll be able to focus less on rote work and more on thinking strategically about how to improve customer experiences and invent new ones. Agents will be teammates that we can call on at various stages of our work, and that will get wiser and more helpful with more experience. If we build and leverage the right agents, it’s going to rapidly accelerate our ability to make customers' lives easier and better every day, and it’s going to make our jobs even more exciting and fun than they are today.

And third, we’re going to keep pushing to operate like the world’s largest start-up-- customer-obsessed, inventive, fast-moving, lean, scrappy, and full of missionaries trying to build something better for customers and a business that outlasts us all. You will continue to see steam and I take actions to help us move faster, have more ownership, and invent more easily. AI will be a substantial catalyst here.

Today, we have over 1,000 Generative AI services and applications in progress or built, but at our scale, that’s a small fraction of what we will ultimately build. We’re going to lean in further in the coming months. We’re going to make it much easier to build agents, and then build (or partner) on several new agents across all of our business units and G&A areas.

As we roll out more Generative AI and agents, it should change the way our work is done. We will need fewer people doing some of the jobs that are being done today, and more people doing other types of jobs. It’s hard to know exactly where this nets out over time, but in the next few years, we expect that this will reduce our total corporate workforce as we get efficiency gains from using AI extensively across the company.

As we go through this transformation together, be curious about AI, educate yourself, attend workshops and take trainings, use and experiment with AI whenever you can, participate in your team’s brainstorms to figure out how to invent for our customers more quickly and expansively, and how to get more done with scrappier teams. When I first started at Amazon in 1997 as an Assistant Product Manager, I worked on leaner teams that got a lot done quickly and where I could have substantial impact. We didn’t have tools resembling anything like Generative AI, but we had broad remits, high ambition, and saw the opportunity to improve (and invent) so many customer experiences. Fast forward 28 years and the most transformative technology since the Internet is here. Those who embrace this change, become conversant in AI, help us build and improve our AI capabilities internally and deliver for customers, will be well-positioned to have high impact and help us reinvent the company.

There's so much more to come with Generative AI. I'm energized by our progress, excited about our plans ahead, and looking forward to partnering with you all as we change what’s possible for our customers, partners, and how we work.

notes.explain: 原文特指 corporate workforce（企业员工总数），并把预期放在未来几年；没有说所有岗位都会消失，也没有给出确定人数或比例。
notes.example: The company expects automation to reduce its corporate workforce over time.

notes.phrase: It’s hard to know exactly where this nets out over time
notes.meaning: 很难确切判断长期下来最终会是什么结果
notes.explain: net out 在这里指各类岗位增减合在一起后的净结果。CEO 表示具体影响尚不确定，不能转述成确定的岗位数字。
notes.example: It’s hard to know exactly where the new process will net out over time.

notes.phrase: use and experiment with AI whenever you can
notes.meaning: 尽可能使用并尝试 AI
notes.explain: 这是面向员工的行动建议；原文还提到学习、参加培训和团队讨论，不等于要求未经审核地把 AI 用于客户交付。
notes.example: We should use and experiment with AI whenever we can, while checking the results.

notes.meaning: 官方原文中的疑似拼写或排版错误
notes.explain: Amazon 的组织领导团队通常写作 S-team；官方网页此处显示 steam。保留原文以便核对，不把这处文字当作正确范例。
notes.example: The S-team will review the proposal.

scenario.title: 同事把企业层面的预测当成了本组裁员通知
english: A teammate read Jassy’s 2025 message and assumes it confirms that their own role will be eliminated.

The message said Amazon expected fewer people in some jobs, more people in other types of jobs, and a smaller total corporate workforce over the next few years. It also said the exact net effect was hard to know.

Explain what the letter did and did not say, then suggest learning about AI and testing one suitable work use with appropriate review. Do not present the company-wide forecast as an individual staffing decision.
chinese: 一位同事读了 Jassy 2025 年的信，便认定自己的岗位已经确定会被取消。
信中说，Amazon 预计部分岗位人数会减少、其他类型的工作会增加，未来几年企业员工总数会减少；同时也承认净影响尚难确切判断。
说明信里说了什么、没有说什么，再建议学习 AI，并在适当审核下试用一个合适的工作场景。不要把公司层面的预测说成个人岗位决定。

firstAttempt.prompt: 同事问，Andy Jassy 的 2025 年员工信有没有承诺 AI 不会让岗位发生变化。请用英文概括信里对岗位数量、影响不确定性的判断，并转述他给员工的建议。
firstAttempt.sample: I understand why you’re concerned about what AI may mean for your role. Jassy said, “We will need fewer people doing some of the jobs that are being done today, and more people doing other types of jobs.” He also said, “It’s hard to know exactly where this nets out over time,” while expecting AI efficiency gains to reduce Amazon’s corporate workforce in the next few years. He encouraged employees to use and experiment with AI whenever they can.
firstAttempt.rationale: 准确说清部分工作减少、另一些工作增加、净影响尚不确定，以及员工学习和尝试 AI 的建议；不把公司预期说成所有岗位都会消失。

words.example: The company expects its corporate workforce to change over time.
words.translation: 公司预计企业员工总数会随时间发生变化。
words.note: 此处 corporate workforce 指企业员工总数，不能扩大为所有合同工或全球岗位的精确统计。

words.example: The company expects efficiency gains from using AI extensively.
words.translation: 公司预计广泛使用 AI 会带来效率提升。
words.note: 原文将效率提升与岗位结构变化联系起来，但没有提供量化比例。

words.meaning: 合并计算后的净结果是
words.collocation: how something nets out over time
words.example: It is hard to know how the changes will net out over time.
words.translation: 很难判断这些变化长期合并起来的净结果。
words.note: 常用于多种相反影响相互抵消后的最终结果。

words.example: We can experiment with the tool on an internal task first.
words.translation: 我们可以先在内部任务中试用这个工具。
words.note: experiment with 表示尝试一种工具或方法；具体使用仍应遵循团队审核要求。

words.example: The letter describes AI as a transformative technology.
words.translation: 这封信把 AI 描述为一种带来重大变化的技术。
words.note: 表示影响深远，不代表每项 AI 应用都已成熟或有效。

words.meaning: 处于有利位置的；更有准备的
words.example: Employees who build AI skills may be well-positioned to contribute.
words.translation: 具备 AI 技能的员工可能更有条件作出贡献。
words.note: 原文描述的是可能更有机会产生影响，不是对职位或晋升的保证。

structure.original: We will need fewer people doing some of the jobs that are being done today, and more people doing other types of jobs.
analysis: We will need 表示对未来需求的判断。
fewer people doing... 与 more people doing... 平行对照两类工作的人数变化。
some...that are being done today 限定为当前正在做的部分工作；原句没有说所有岗位都会消失。
structure.transfer: As customer demand shifts, our team may need fewer manual status checks and more time for complex support cases.

rewrite.bad: AI will eliminate every job next year, so there is no point in learning it.
rewrite.good: Jassy said Amazon expected fewer people in some jobs and more people in other types of jobs. He expected AI-related efficiency gains to reduce the total corporate workforce over the next few years, while noting that the exact net impact was hard to know. He encouraged employees to learn about and experiment with AI.
rewrite.translation: Jassy 表示，Amazon 预计部分岗位人数会减少、其他类型岗位会增加。他预计 AI 带来的效率提升会在未来几年减少企业员工总数，同时承认净影响尚难确切判断。他鼓励员工学习并尝试 AI。
rewrite.pattern: [Source] expects fewer people in [some roles] and more in [other work]. The exact impact is hard to know, so [measured next step].

cloze.prompt: The email expected fewer people in some jobs and more people in ___ types of jobs.
cloze.why: 原文用 other types 与 some of the jobs 对照，说明工作类型会发生变化。

cloze.prompt: It’s hard to know exactly where this ___ out over time.
cloze.why: net out 指不同影响合并后的最终结果；原文主语 this，所以用 nets。

cloze.prompt: Employees were encouraged to use and ___ with AI whenever they can.
cloze.why: use and experiment with 是原信给员工的行动建议。

dictation.text: It’s hard to know exactly where this nets out over time, but in the next few years, we expect that this will reduce our total corporate workforce as we get efficiency gains from using AI extensively across the company.
dictation.label: 听写 1 · 岗位影响与不确定性
dictation.why: 这段保留了时间范围、企业员工总数和影响不确定性；不能把预测改成确定人数。

dictation.text: Those who embrace this change, become conversant in AI, help us build and improve our AI capabilities internally and deliver for customers, will be well-positioned to have high impact and help us reinvent the company.
dictation.label: 听写 2 · 员工如何为变化作准备
dictation.why: 听出学习 AI、改善内部能力和服务客户之间的联系。

apply.prompt: 用英文概括信里给员工的建议，不要承诺一定保住岗位。
apply.sample: Jassy encouraged employees to learn about AI, experiment with it, and help improve the company’s AI capabilities and customer experiences.

translationPractice.prompt: 我们将需要更少的人从事目前的一些工作，也会需要更多的人从事其他类型的工作。
translationPractice.answer: We will need fewer people doing some of the jobs that are being done today, and more people doing other types of jobs.
translationPractice.why: 保留 fewer...and more... 的对照，不把岗位变化概括成所有岗位都消失。

translationPractice.prompt: 很难确切判断这件事长期下来最终会是什么结果。
translationPractice.answer: It’s hard to know exactly where this nets out over time.
translationPractice.why: net out 表示多种岗位变化合并后的净影响。

translationPractice.prompt: 尽可能使用并尝试 AI。
translationPractice.answer: Use and experiment with AI whenever you can.
translationPractice.why: 这是原信明确给员工的建议；实际应用仍需遵守团队流程。

choice.prompt: 关于 Andy Jassy 对岗位影响的描述，哪一项忠实保留了原信的范围和不确定性？
options: Amazon promised that no current roles would change if employees attended AI training.
Amazon expected fewer people in some jobs, more in other types of jobs, and a smaller corporate workforce over the next few years; the exact net effect was hard to know.
Amazon announced that exactly 15% of all employees would be laid off by the end of the year.
choice.why: 原文描述部分工作减少、其他工作增加，并预计未来几年企业员工总数下降；没有给出固定裁员比例，也没有保证岗位不变。

output.prompt: 团队想用生成式 AI 总结内部服务工单，另一位同事担心摘要出错。请用英文回应顾虑，建议先小范围试用并人工核对，再分享准确性和节省时间的结果后决定是否扩大。
output.sample: I understand why you’re concerned about errors in AI summaries. Could we test the tool on a small set of internal tickets and have an agent review every summary before it is used? Let’s share what we learn about accuracy and time saved before we expand the test.
check: 是否回应了对 AI 摘要出错的具体担忧？
是否把试用限制在小范围内部工单并安排人工复核？
是否先分享准确性和节省时间的证据，再决定是否扩大？
